title: PortPlan
description:
How one feature spec goes into one host model. Written by the plan node (stage 2) after reading the host checkout at `host_revision`, and read by the integration node (stage 3), which treats it as authoritative on WHERE and HOW to hook. The feature spec stays authoritative on WHAT the mechanism is, so a plan never restates pseudocode.

Nothing here may mention a resource budget. Only the DSE stage applies constraints (docs/stages.md), so this document has no storage split and no allowance. What it does carry is the host's own sizing knobs (`host_knobs`) and what the host's structures cost at any setting of them (`host_storage`). Those are facts about the tree, not decisions: every host knob ships at the clean tree's value, and choosing any other value is stage 4's job alone. Stage 4 cannot pay for a feature by shrinking a host structure it cannot move, which is why the plan exposes them. `additionalProperties` is false throughout, as much to stop a budget smuggled in under an invented field name as for typo-catching: a budget there fails validation instead of reaching the integrator as an instruction.

feature_name.description: Must equal the feature spec's `feature_name`, e.g. 'sr'. The pair (feature_name, host) names this plan and its test plan.

host.description: Which performance model this plan is for: 'champsim', 'gem5', or a fixture host's name.

host_revision.description: The exact commit the plan was written against, so a plan can never be silently applied to a different tree than the one whose hook points were read. A checkout with no VCS records whatever identifier reproduces it (a release tarball name, a fixture path plus the repo commit that last touched it).

spec_inputs_used.description: Echo of the spec's `source.inputs_used`. Ablation 2 compares two ports of the same feature into the same host; without this the two plans are indistinguishable after the fact.

structure.description: The module or class shape the port takes in this host.

choice.description: The shape chosen and why it fits this host, in terms of facts read from the checkout (e.g. 'one ChampSim module owning a base TAGE-SC-L member plus the sR term, because a branch_predictor list keeps only the last module's prediction').

rejected_alternatives.description: The other options hosts/<host>/NOTES.md records, each with the reason it lost. May be empty only when the host genuinely offers one hook shape. Stage 3 is forbidden from re-litigating these; an alternative that turns out to be necessary is a plan revision, not an integrator decision.

source.description: Where the alternative is described, e.g. 'hosts/gem5/NOTES.md option 2'.

hook_points.description: Every site the port touches, in the host checkout. Referenced by id from `spec_map` and `steps`.

id.description: Stable handle for this site. Unique within the plan; JSON Schema cannot express key uniqueness, so the plan checks enforce it.

file.description: Path relative to the host checkout root.

symbol.description: The class, function, or build target the change lands in. For a new file, the symbol it will define.

observed.description: What the site does today, read from the checkout. Required when `action` is 'modify': the planner may only claim a hook point it actually looked at, and the integrator needs to recognise the code it is about to change. Meaningless for 'create'.

change.description: What goes here, in enough detail that the integrator does not re-derive the decision. Behaviour of the mechanism itself belongs in the spec, not here.

spec_map.description: Spec item -> code site. The coverage check's principal input: every `/state/N` and `/algorithms/N` in the spec must appear here, or the plan fails before integration starts. Spec parameters are covered by `knobs`, `host_interfaces` needs by `interface_resolutions`; mapping those here as well is allowed but not required.

spec_item.description: The `name` at that pointer, copied verbatim. Redundant on purpose: code cross-checks it, so an off-by-one pointer cannot satisfy coverage while pointing the integrator at the wrong element.

hook_ids.description: Which hook points realize this spec item.

realization.description: How the code at those sites realizes this item: the data structure it becomes, the call it is made from. Not a restatement of the spec's pseudocode.

interface_resolutions.description: One entry per `host_interfaces[]` need in the spec, including the ones this host meets exactly. Recording the met ones too is what lets the coverage check demand a decision for every need rather than only for the needs the planner happened to notice were hard.

spec_pointer.description: Pointer to the need in the spec.

need.description: The spec's `need` text, copied verbatim; cross-checked against the pointer.

status.description: 'exact': the host provides it as the spec describes. 'fallback': it provides a substitute. 'unavailable': neither, and the port is degraded here.

resolution.description: What the port actually does: the host facility used for 'exact', the substitute and how it is derived otherwise.

rationale.description: Why, grounded in what was read in the checkout or in hosts/<host>/NOTES.md.

fidelity_note.description: What the port loses relative to the paper, and how that could show up in the results. Required for 'fallback' and 'unavailable'; this is the text the integrator copies into PORT_NOTES.md, so a deviation is recorded once, at the point it was decided.

knobs.description: One entry per spec `parameters[]` entry. Nothing tunable may be hard-coded: a parameter missing here is a parameter stage 4 cannot search.

spec_parameter.description: The spec's parameter `name`, copied verbatim; cross-checked against the pointer.

macro.description: The #define `dse.params_header_from_spec` emits for this parameter: literally 'SR_' plus the spec parameter name upper-cased. The prefix is fixed in code for every feature, not derived from `feature_name`. Stage 4 mutates that one header, so a knob wired to any other name is invisible to the search.

host_knob.description: The host-native knob the macro drives: a SimObject Param, a constexpr, an environment variable, a config JSON key.

default.description: The value the port ships. Must equal the spec's default for this parameter; code cross-checks it, because a port that quietly ships a different default measures something the spec does not describe.

host_knobs.description: The host's own sizing knobs: every define, parameter or constant that sets the size of a host structure the port leaves in place (table entry counts, tag widths, counter widths, bank counts). Stage 4 reads these from the same generated params header as the feature's knobs, under `HOST_` macros, so it can trade host storage against the feature's. Each one ships at the clean tree's value, so with every host knob at its default the host is bit-identical to the recorded baseline and G2 is unaffected. Record the knob and its legal range; never a smaller or larger value. May be empty only for a host with no resizable structure, and then `host_storage` is omitted.

name.description: Lower-case handle, usually the host symbol lower-cased, e.g. 'logg'. `host_storage` formulas refer to the knob by this name.

macro.description: Literally 'HOST_' plus `name` upper-cased. This is the #define stage 4 mutates in the params header; code cross-checks it.

host_symbol.description: The host's own identifier this knob replaces, e.g. the macro 'LOGG'.

file.description: Path, relative to the checkout root, of the file that defines `host_symbol`.

observed.description: The line in `file` that sets `host_symbol` today, copied verbatim, including its value. Code checks that it occurs in the checkout and holds `default`, so a plan can only expose a knob somebody read.

default.description: The value the clean tree uses, exactly. Not a proposal.

range.description: Legal values, in the spec's range syntax: '[lo, hi]' or '[lo, hi] pow2'. Legal means the host still builds and runs correctly at every value in it, so read what else the symbol feeds (index widths, shifts, derived sizes) before widening it. Include values on both sides of the default: below it is how a tight allowance pays for the feature, and above it is how a generous one spends spare storage on the host.

description.description: What the knob sizes, in terms of the host's structures, and anything that limits it (e.g. 'the two shortest-history tables are half size, so it must stay at least 2').

host_storage.description: The host's accounted storage, as formulas over `host_knobs[].name`, so stage 4 can cost a candidate that shrinks the host. Required whenever `host_knobs` is non-empty. This is accounting, not a budget: it says what the host costs, never what it may cost.

baseline_bits.description: The host's storage in bits at the clean tree's values, as the host's own accounting reports it. Measured, not computed from `terms`: code evaluates the terms at the defaults and requires them to reproduce this number.

measured_by.description: The command, or the host's accounting function, whose output gave `baseline_bits`.

terms.description: One entry per host structure, following the host's own accounting. Their sum is the host's storage. A structure no knob resizes is still a term, with a constant formula, so that the sum reproduces `baseline_bits`.

structure.description: What the term counts, e.g. 'tagged tables, high banks'.

formula.description: Bits, as arithmetic over host knob names and numbers: + - * / // % ** << >>, parentheses, and min, max, log2, ceil, floor, abs, int. Never ^ for a power; Python reads it as XOR.

feature_enable.description: The one knob that turns the whole feature on. Gate condition G2 is a claim about this knob, so the plan has to state the claim before the integrator can be held to it.

name.description: The knob's name, exactly as the spec names it (e.g. 'TINYSC_ENABLE').

macro.description: Present when the enable knob is also a spec parameter, and therefore also a define in the generated params header.

default_off.description: The mechanism that makes off the default, such that an unconfigured build of the host reproduces the baseline without anyone remembering to set anything.

off_path.description: What executes with the knob off, and why that is bit-identical to the recorded baseline rather than merely close. G2 checks this claim against measured metrics.

steps.description: Ordered, individually buildable increments. Each one must leave the host compiling, so a failure has a small blast radius and the debug node has a last-known-good point to bisect to.

verify.description: How the integrator knows this increment landed: a shell command, or the id of a test-plan `correctness[]` entry.

risks.description: What could go wrong in this port specifically. A generic risk is noise; the useful entries are the ones that name a host fact.

detected_by.description: The id of the test-plan entry that would catch this, if one does. A risk nothing detects is worth knowing about as such.

open_questions.description: What the spec left unresolved, plus the reading this plan takes. Unlike the spec's `open_questions`, which are bare strings, a plan's must carry a decision: the planner has the host in front of it and the integrator does not get to re-decide silently. A deviation from the assumption goes in PORT_NOTES.md.

assumption.description: The reading the port implements until told otherwise.

cost_if_wrong.description: What has to change if the assumption is wrong, which is what decides whether this is worth resolving before integration or after.

spec_pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the feature spec, e.g. '/state/0'. The plan checks resolve it; a pointer that does not resolve is a planning failure, not an integration surprise.

hook_id_list.description: Ids of `hook_points` entries. Every id must name one; code checks the reference.

binding.description: How a value reaches the host. 'compile_time_define' needs a rebuild per value, which stage 4 pays for on every candidate; 'python_param' and 'runtime_env' do not.
